title: Cocharacter orbit-extension predicate and parabolic limit subfunctor
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $G$ a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to G$ be a group-scheme homomorphism, with $\mathbf G_m$ and $\mathbf A^1$ the affine test schemes of [def-sc-gm-ga]. For a commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and $g\in G(A)$, an orbit extension is a $k$-morphism $q:\operatorname{Spec}A\times_k\mathbf A^1_k\to G$ such that its restriction along $\operatorname{id}\times(\mathbf G_m\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1)$ equals $(a,t)\mapsto\lambda(t)g(a)\lambda(t)^{-1}$. Define $P_\lambda(A)=\{g\in G(A):\text{there exists such an orbit extension }q\}$. Equivalently, the corresponding $A$-orbit extends to an $A$-morphism $\mathbf A^1_A\to G_A$. The condition is tested on every commutative $k$-algebra, including nonreduced algebras. These are definitions only; no representability, smoothness or connectedness assertion is included.

This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse moduli scheme. Supporting input: Projective geometric quotients of closed stable loci for PGL. Affine-chart proof of the projective PGL quotient: Power lifting and finite generation for PGL invariants. Supporting argument: Haboush symmetric-power lifting for a trivial quotient representation. Supporting representation-theoretic input: Steinberg endomorphisms detect a nonzero fixed vector. Supporting Self-duality of rho section modules at characteristic-dependent weights. Supporting input: Positive-characteristic simplicity step, using irreducibility of the Steinberg induced module rather than assuming self-duality. Numerical input to the dimension comparison: Weyl dimension of the induced module. Supporting Integral Euler character of arbitrary flag line bundles. Section 22d, proof of Theorem 22.50, p.480: general fixed-point input, stated here in its integral equivariant form; Example 22.36, pp.473--474, for formal characters. WANTED: Nielsen 1974 general fixed-point theorem and Iversen 1976, 9.4; neither document is present. The integral formulation is an agent-supplied supporting statement. Supporting input: Section 22d, proof of Theorem 22.50, p.480: agent-supplied concentration prerequisite, not the numerical fixed-point formula itself. WANTED: Thomason, Une formule de Lefschetz en K-theorie equivariante algebrique, Duke Math. J. 53 (1986), concentration theorem; not present locally. No proof of concentration is claimed to occur in Milne. Supporting step: The concentration theorem's nonfixed-locus annihilation argument in the proof of the item. Geometric input to nonfixed-locus annihilation: invariant affine strata of the reduction, before the Laurent-coefficient and localization arguments. Supporting normal-case neighbourhood input used after passing to the invariant smooth locus, before removing one affine open in the Noetherian induction. Supporting proof input: Linearize the normal quasi-projective neighborhood by an immersion into projective space of a rational representation. Supporting line-bundle prerequisite: replace an ample invertible module by a positive tensor power carrying an algebraic G-linearization, before choosing invariant sections. Supporting Picard input: a tensor exponent uniform over the generic residue fields of all normal components, before applying the generic-line pullback criterion. Supporting base-change input: Brion Lemma 2.3, pullback Pic(G) to Pic(G_K), specialized using Remark 2.2(v). Supporting substep: Brion, On Linearization of Line Bundles, Lemma 2.3 proof, printed p.118, the Pic(G/B) and root-datum paragraph, citing Iversen 1976 Proposition 5.2 and Theorem 5.3. The explicit split Schubert-boundary basis and its scalar-extension form are the geometric input unpacked here; also Milne Lemma 18.21, printed p.392, the split affine-cell argument. The statement concerns split groups over arbitrary fields, not only algebraically closed fields. Supporting geometry: the split Bruhat stratification before the boundary-divisor argument; Milne Theorems 21.73 and 21.80. Supporting input: Chapter 21 standing arbitrary field, printed p.424; Proposition 21.1, p.424 (constant Weyl group and rational representatives); Summary 21.41, p.436; the fixed-scheme paragraph immediately before Proposition 21.70, p.446. Scalar-extension stability of split Borel pairs is used throughout Section 21h. The fixed-scheme assertion is scheme-theoretic, not just a statement about rational points. Supporting substep: Theorem 21.32 and Corollary 21.33, printed pp.434-435, together with Proposition 21.29, pp.433-434. Applied to a Borel containing the scalar extension of V to an algebraic closure: all geometric Borels through the split torus descend and are regular cocharacter limit subgroups. This is a containment input without a Borel or maximality hypothesis on V.
